title: Introduce private-controlplane endpoint rotation and graceful peering teardown
author: Lena Koh
description: Motivation: Private control plane customers running multi-AZ or multi-account topologies need safer lifecycle operations for control-plane VPC endpoints and peerings during upgrades and infrastructure rotation. This PR adds a Terraform module and supporting Helm hooks that implement coordinated endpoint rotation, graceful peering teardown with traffic drain, and a small operator that sequences DNS switchovers to minimize request loss. Summary of changes: 1) terraform/modules/controlplane-endpoint: new module that supports ephemeral endpoint attachments, tagging for ownership, and a rotation plan resource that produces stepwise actions to re-attach endpoints in a safe ordering across AZs; 2) helm/charts/private-installer/templates/hooks: pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks that call the endpoint-rotation job and validate DNS propagation; 3) installer/bin/endpoint-rotation-operator: a lightweight controller (Go, ~420 LOC) invoked as a Job during upgrades; it performs readiness probes, issues AWS route updates or on-prem route table changes, and emits structured status for the console; 4) examples/upgrade-playbooks: a curated playbook and CI job recipe that demonstrates performing a canary rotation to a single AZ before full rollout; 5) tests/terraform: unit-style plan assertions and a simulated peering teardown acceptance test that verifies no connections dropped beyond a short tolerated window. Backwards compatibility: module exposes flags to operate in read-only dry-run mode and to disable automated teardown for customers that prefer manual steps. Rollback strategy: the operator includes an explicit reversal routine that rebinds previous endpoints, flushes KV caches via API, and re-runs DNS roll-forward checks. Related work: Linear ENG-9721 (control-plane lifecycle), ENG-10014 (dns propagation improvements). This is not a breaking change. The description below includes a high-level commit summary, changed files, CI status, reviewers, and the review conversation. Carefully tested in staging with full multi-AZ simulation and validated with canary traffic.
commits: feat(module): add controlplane-endpoint terraform module with rotation plan generation
feat(operator): add endpoint-rotation-operator job and basic controller loop
chore(helm): add pre/post upgrade hooks for endpoint rotation and dns validation
tests: add simulated peering teardown acceptance test and terraform plan checks
docs: add upgrade playbook and operator runbook
release_notes: Added controlplane endpoint rotation module and operator to enable safe endpoint rotation and graceful peering teardown during upgrades. Includes Helm hooks, example playbook, and rollback routine.
review_comments: Priya Shah (reviewer): The operator should expose a dry-run mode and a configurable drain timeout. Can you add a command-line flag instead of env-only?
Lena Koh (author): Added --dry-run and --drain-timeout flags to the operator binary and documented them in README. Updated helm values to accept args for the job invocation.
Daniel Park (reviewer): Terraform plan generation looks good. Suggest adding a state tag to endpoints to help with cleanup race conditions.
Lena Koh (author): Added endpoint_state tag and a reconciler loop in the operator to garbage collect orphaned ephemeral endpoints after a grace period. The reconcilier is opt-in via module variable.

Ethan Martinez (reviewer): CI flaked once on the plan assertions in the simulated teardown job. Re-ran and it passed. Please include a note in the runbook about transient failures and the expected retry semantics.
Lena Koh (author): Added runbook note and tuned plan assertions to be tolerant of controlplane metadata drift under simulated failover.
Priya Shah (approver): Approved after the operator flags and tagging changes. Verified staging runbook steps and canary traffic results.
test_summary: Simulated multi-AZ deployment with 3 AZs. Canary run: rotated endpoints in AZ-b as canary, validated <0.5% request error delta, then rolled full. Acceptance test asserts DNS TTL switch and route table updates. Operator reversal test rebinds previous endpoints within 30s in simulated environment.
operational_impact: This change touches private control plane VPC endpoints and peering workflows. Customers with strict manual change controls can set module.auto_teardown = false. Operator runs as a Job during upgrades; resource usage is minimal (single CPU, 128Mi memory) and short-lived.
migration_steps: 1) Add terraform/modules/controlplane-endpoint to your installer root module and set endpoint_rotation.enabled = true. 2) Update Helm values to point at the new operator image and enable pre-upgrade hooks. 3) Run canary by setting upgrade.playbook.canary_az and validate metrics. 4) If errors observed, run the operator with --dry-run=false --rollback to rebind previous endpoints.
notes: Follow up PR planned to add GCP/On-Prem route table adapters and a metrics exporter for the operator. Also considering adding an opt-in post-rotation cache flush API call for Redwood serving nodes.
changelog: feature: controlplane endpoint rotation and graceful peering teardown. operator + terraform module + helm hooks + runbook.
